dedupe_keys.name: stars4water precipitation deficit for selected river basins in europe

description: The STARS4Water project deposits precipitation-deficit indicators for selected European river basins. Its Zenodo description defines each day's deficit as accumulated potential evaporation minus precipitation from 1 April, reset to zero when negative, with a seasonal maximum for April through September. Future evaporation is estimated by the Priestley-Taylor method from pan-European climate variables. A public ZIP is labelled CC BY 4.0. A drought or irrigation simulation could use the deficit to compare basin stress across years or climate scenarios. It is an index of meteorological demand, not actual evaporation or directly measured soil-water shortage. The own page warns that an April start may misrepresent southern basins and earlier climate-driven drought onset. The ZIP was not opened, so its basin list, units, grids and time horizon remain unverified. Related upstream Copernicus input terms are separate. Round one rejected this water resource as not industry-first, leaving it for a water review.
